Subject: Embeddings integration  post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for your time today  great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- What we heard from Acme:
  - Primary use case: semantic search over product docs + reranking for recommendations.
  - Current embeddings: vendor "VectraEmbed" (proprietary) at 2048 dims; sizing and latency issues observed at scale.
  - Migration goals: reduce cost per query, improve recall on short queries, preserve existing nearest-neighbor behavior.

- Redwood recommended approach (high-level):
  1) Start with a 1536-d embedding (we've found good cost/quality tradeoff for product-doc style corpora).
  2) Apply L2 normalization at index time (store unit vectors) and use cosine similarity for scoring  preserves nearest-neighbor ranking and works well with FAISS/Annoy/GALEN.
  3) Batch embedding calls during ingest (recommended batch size 128 depending on average doc length); for short strings 256 is efficient, for long documents use 648.
  4) Keep a migration toggle (feature flag) to A/B test new vectors vs VectraEmbed outputs; run offline evals on your golden queries.
  5) Consider a lightweight reranker (cross-encoder) for top-K re-ranking to recover precision for recommendation flows.

Technical next steps we propose: 
- Dev task: SDK eval + auth: Dev will try a small PoC using our Python SDK, auth via API key + role-restricted token for ingest jobs.
- Data: Acme to share a ~5k sample CSV of documents (text, doc_id).
- Migration checklist: we attached a short checklist (redwood_embeddings_migration_checklist.pdf) and will share a Drive folder with scripts.
- PoC timeline: 1 week for PoC ingestion & evaluation, then lift to pilot if results look good.

Can you confirm the sample dataset share and whether you prefer 1536 or want to test both 1536 and 2048 in the PoC?

Hi Alex  thanks for the call and the questions. A few technical answers and concrete PoC plan: 

1) Dimensions: Yes  we recommend starting with 1536 as the default (good balance of cost vs quality). For the PoC we can generate both 1536 and 2048 for a small subset (1k documents) to run direct A/B offline on your golden queries. That will tell us if 2048 yields a material recall uplift worth the extra cost.

2) Batching & throughput: Redwood's hosted embedding endpoint supports concurrent requests and we also support large single-request batches. Practical guidance: aim for logical batch sizes of 6456 items per API call. For Spark micro-batches you can bundle rows into 128-item batches; if average doc text length is small (<200 tokens) you can increase to 256512. We will provide a sample batching helper in the PoC repo.

3) Normalization & similarity: Perform L2 normalization at index-time (store unit vectors) and use cosine similarity on the query-side. If you use FAISS with inner-product search over normalized vectors it is equivalent to cosine ranking. We will provide scripts to normalize and reindex.

4) Auth / routing: Use short-lived service tokens issued by Redwood's admin console (or our OAuth flow). Recommended pattern: 
   - Create a service account in your org admin console with embedding:write scope.
   - Use rotating short-lived tokens (1h) issued via your CI/ETL credential manager (Hashicorp Vault / GCP KMS).
   - For high-throughput bulk ingest, split workload across N workers with separate tokens to avoid single-token throttling.

5) Migration approach:
   - Offload 1k sample to PoC; generate 1536 and 2048 vectors for same docs.
   - Run offline NN evaluation (recall@10, MRR) on golden queries.
   - If 1536 matches or outperforms, proceed to full reindex (incremental) with feature-flag rollout.

6) Costs & limits: For planning assume 1536 vectors cost ~0.7x of your current per-vector spend (depends on provider SKU). We'll surface precise per-100k numbers in the PoC report. Our public rate limits are flexible for paid pilots; we'll coordinate a temporary bump for your pilot window.

I'll drop a small helper script and batching example to the Drive folder today. If you can share the sample CSV and a list of golden queries (1020), I'll run the A/B and share results.

Cheers,
